groups.title: Cloud Computing Models
groups.question: Explain how the cloud service models differ and how AWS spreads its infrastructure around the world.

followUps.IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS Explained: How does your share of operational work change as you move from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS, and when would you pick each?
followUps.AWS Global Infrastructure: Why would you spread a workload across several Availability Zones, and when would you go further and use more than one Region?

groups.title: IAM Core Concepts
groups.question: Explain how AWS decides who can do what in an account, and who is responsible for securing which parts.

followUps.Users, Groups, Roles, and Policies: When would you give a workload an IAM role instead of creating an IAM user with access keys, and why?
followUps.Shared Responsibility Model: If you run a database on EC2, which security tasks are still yours that AWS does not handle for you?

groups.title: Core Services: EC2 and S3
groups.question: Walk through how you would choose compute and object storage for a new application on AWS.

followUps.EC2 Instance Types and Pricing: How would you decide between a general-purpose, compute-optimized, or memory-optimized instance for a workload?
followUps.S3 Buckets and Storage Classes: How would you pick an S3 storage class for data whose access drops off over time?

groups.title: AWS CLI and Well-Architected
groups.question: Explain how you would work with AWS day to day and how you would judge whether an architecture is good.

followUps.AWS CLI and Console Basics: Why is the CLI more useful than the console when you need repeatable work or need to debug a broken deployment?
followUps.AWS Well-Architected Framework: How would you use the Well-Architected pillars to spot risks in a design before it goes to production?
